item.title: Tesla and SpaceX form special committees to study a merger, Musk calls it 'a good idea'
item.description: On SpaceX's earnings call, Elon Musk confirmed both companies have set up committees of independent directors to explore a combination. No terms are agreed, and Tesla shareholders would face a high approval bar.

item.title: Tesla Q3 2026 earnings tonight: the numbers and questions that matter
item.description: Tesla reports third-quarter results after the market closes today. Here is what Wall Street expects and which topics will decide how the stock reacts.

item.title: Tesla's 'flying' Roadster: what we actually know about the thruster-powered supercar
item.description: Tesla finally showed its next-generation Roadster, complete with cold-gas thrusters that let it hop over other cars. Here are the specs, trims, deposits and the open questions.

item.title: Tesla Japan still aims to launch FSD this year, but admits the deadline is tough
item.description: Tesla Japan's president says the company is making every effort to launch FSD (Supervised) before the end of 2026. Approval depends on regulators, and a Cybercab service is a separate question.

item.title: Tesla's 2026 shareholder meeting is set for December 3, with no merger vote on the ballot
item.description: Musk, Robyn Denholm and JB Straubel are up for re-election. There is no new pay package for Musk and no merger proposal. Here is what shareholders will vote on.

item.title: Tesla Optimus production: several hundred robots a week now, 1,000 targeted by year-end
item.description: Reports say Fremont is building several hundred Optimus humanoid robots a week on former Model S and X lines, with an internal target of 1,000 a week by the end of 2026.

item.title: Six-seat Model Y L: US delivery estimates now stretch to March 2027
item.description: New US orders for the long-wheelbase Model Y L Launch Series now show January to March 2027. Here is what the six-seater costs and what you get.

item.title: Will Tesla and SpaceX merge? What Barclays expects, and what is actually confirmed
item.description: A Barclays note suggests a Tesla-SpaceX deal could be announced before Tesla's December shareholder meeting. Nothing has been agreed. Here is the scenario and the facts.

item.title: Model Y beats the VW Golf: Tesla has Germany's best-selling car in September
item.description: With 8,038 registrations, the Model Y was the most popular new car in Germany in September. Tesla's German sales nearly quadrupled, helped by a new EV subsidy.

item.title: Where Tesla Robotaxi operates now: six cities without a safety driver
item.description: From Austin to Tampa, Tesla's Robotaxi service is live in six US cities without a safety driver, plus the Bay Area with one. Here is the full list and what is coming next.

item.title: Tesla in China: September retail sales fall 9%, but Shanghai exports jump 58%
item.description: Giga Shanghai shipped 95,366 cars in September, up 5%, as exports made up for weaker domestic demand. It is the fourth straight month of falling retail sales in China.

item.title: Tesla starts rolling out FSD v14.3.11: what's new and who gets it first
item.description: The latest version of Full Self-Driving (Supervised) is reaching early testers on software 2026.33.5. HW4 cars get v14.3.11; HW3 cars get a 'Lite' version.

item.title: Tesla asked for eight more weeks to answer NHTSA on the Cybercab. It got 30 days
item.description: The US regulator has moved Tesla's deadline to October 30. Its 21 questions cover everything from mirrors and brakes to why Tesla never applied for an exemption.

item.title: Tesla Energy deploys 13.7 GWh in Q3: growth continues, but slower than hoped
item.description: Tesla's battery storage business grew almost 10% from a year ago, yet missed analyst expectations by more than 2 GWh. Here is what is behind the numbers.

item.title: Tesla UK sales nearly double in September, Model 3 is Britain's top electric car
item.description: Tesla registered 15,875 cars in the UK in September, its best month in at least a year and a half. The Model 3 led the EV charts, with the Model Y in second place.

item.title: Tesla delivers 486,532 cars in Q3 2026, beating Wall Street's estimate by 24,500
item.description: Deliveries were slightly lower than a year ago but well above what analysts expected, and Tesla sold more cars than it built. Energy storage was the weak spot.

item.title: Tesla sales rebound in Europe: France up 62%, Sweden up 38% in September
item.description: After two years of decline, Tesla's European registrations are climbing again. Early September data from France, Sweden and Norway all point up.

item.title: Tesla Roadster reveal pushed back two weeks to October 15, blamed on the weather
item.description: The long-awaited Roadster unveiling in Waco, Texas, has moved from October 1 to October 15. Tesla says the event can only be held outdoors and severe conditions were forecast.

item.title: Tesla update 2026.38: smarter headlights, Supercharger site maps and Grok out of beta
item.description: Tesla's latest software update brings adaptive headlight leveling, a live map of selected Supercharger sites and better visuals. Here is what is new and which cars get it.

item.title: Tesla lines up $30 billion in new credit as spending on factories climbs
item.description: A new set of credit facilities gives Tesla about $25 billion more borrowing room than before. It has not drawn on them, but the size says a lot about its spending plans.

item.title: Croatia approves Tesla FSD, but the EU-wide vote slips to December at the earliest
item.description: FSD (Supervised) is now approved in eight European countries. The bloc-wide decision that many expected in October is now not expected before December.

item.title: Tesla opens its Semi factory in Nevada and starts series deliveries
item.description: Nine years after its unveiling, the Tesla Semi is in series production. The new Nevada plant is built for up to 50,000 trucks a year, with Europe due in 2027.

item.title: Ordering a Tesla in the US now? Model 3 and Model Y deliveries slip into 2027
item.description: Tesla's US configurator shows no 2026 delivery slots left for the Model 3 Rear-Wheel Drive, and Model Y waits now stretch to January. Here are the current prices and estimates.

item.title: Czechia becomes seventh EU country to allow Tesla FSD, with an EU-wide vote in sight
item.description: The Czech transport ministry has recognized the Dutch approval of FSD (Supervised). An EU-wide vote could follow, but it needs a large qualified majority.

item.title: Tesla Energy lands 3 GWh Megapack deal for Italian battery projects
item.description: Italian developer Zhero and H1 Holdings will buy 3 GWh of Tesla Megapacks under long-term contracts. It is another sign that grid batteries are becoming one of Tesla's steadiest businesses.

item.title: Tesla takes the Cybercab on tour in Japan: Tokyo, Osaka and Nagoya
item.description: After its Austin launch, the Cybercab heads to Asia for a series of public displays. There are no rides or sales in Japan yet; it is about putting the robotaxi in front of the public.

item.title: Tesla Cybercab specs explained: battery, range, weight and why it skips AC charging
item.description: A small battery, a light body and DC-only charging: the Cybercab's numbers show a car built for one job. Here is what is inside and what it tells us about Tesla's robotaxi plans.

item.title: Slovenia approves Tesla FSD Supervised: where in Europe you can use it now
item.description: Slovenia has become the sixth EU country to allow Tesla's FSD (Supervised). Here is the full list, how the approvals work and what European owners should know.

item.title: More than 73,000 people raise their hand to buy Cybercabs for fleet use
item.description: Tesla opened an interest form for businesses that want to buy and run Cybercab fleets. The number of clicks is big, but it is a signal of curiosity, not a pile of orders.

item.title: US safety regulator probes how Tesla certified the Cybercab, one day after launch
item.description: NHTSA has opened an audit into Tesla's claim that the steering-wheel-free Cybercab meets every federal safety standard. Here is what the agency wants to know and why it matters.
